result.title: CSV ledger aggregation pattern (read export.json params first)
result.content:
Task pattern: "total amount of sales rows in ledger.csv export".
Steps: ALWAYS read export.json first — it holds parser params (encoding, delimiter, preamble_lines, file). Do not assume UTF-8/comma/no-preamble: seen cases with {"encoding":"utf-16","delimiter":"\t","preamble_lines":2}.
Call parse_csv(path, encoding=export.encoding, delimiter=export.delimiter, skip_lines=export.preamble_lines). Note: a raw tab in JSON makes the parser emit "\t" which fails with TypeError "delimiter must be a 1-character string" — pass delimiter as the two-character escape "\t" (backslash-t) so it decodes to a real tab.
ledger.csv columns = category,amount; rows alternate sales/refund. "total amount of sales rows" = SUM(amount) over rows where category=="sales" (a sum, not a row count). Example: sales 12,30,48,66 -> 156. Amounts may be strings in the raw rows; cast/round to number.
Always emit result as {"answer": number}.

result.title: experience tool usage quirks
result.content: experience `put` requires a non-empty `id` string; omitting it fails with {"error":"KeyError: 'id'"} even though the schema lists id as optional. Always pass op,id,title,content. Reusing an existing id fully replaces (bumps version). Use op:"search" (query, or empty) to list entries, op:"get" with id to read one, op:"delete" with id to remove.

args.title: CSV ledger sales total (read export.json parser params first)
args.content:
Task pattern: compute "total amount of sales rows in ledger.csv export" -> return {"answer": number}. It is a SUM of the amount column over sales rows, NOT a row count.

Applicability: only for a ledger.csv governed by an export.json in the workspace. Parser params VARY per export - never assume utf-8/comma/no-preamble. (An earlier note hard-coded those defaults; the observed export.json was {"encoding":"utf-16","delimiter":"\t","preamble_lines":2,"file":"ledger.csv"}, so a default parse_csv raised UnicodeDecodeError byte 0xff and would also have mis-split tab fields.)

Steps:
1. read_file export.json to get file, encoding, delimiter, preamble_lines.
2. parse_csv(path=export.file, encoding=export.encoding, delimiter=<tab>, skip_lines=export.preamble_lines).
   - delimiter must be EXACTLY 1 character, else TypeError 'delimiter must be a 1-character string'. For a tab export pass a single tab (write \t in the tool-call JSON) so it decodes to one tab; a multi-character value such as a tab+newline fails. (No evidence that plain \t fails or that a literal backslash-t text is required.)
   - skip_lines must match preamble_lines (observed 2), else preamble/header rows leak into the data.
3. parse_csv rows have columns category,amount (amounts may be strings, e.g. "12"); rows alternate sales/refund. Sum amount where category=='sales'.

Observed example: sales 12,30,48,66 -> 156.
Always emit {"answer": number}.
